subject: Post-call recap: HealthTech private VPC/disconnected deployment (network & compliance needs)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthtech.com>, IT Security <security@healthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: HealthTech private VPC/disconnected deployment (network & compliance needs)

Hi Alex / Security team,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap of what we heard and the suggested next steps. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Key pain points / drivers:
- Data residency + regulatory control for patient PII (HIPAA + regional controls).
- Requirement for an air-gapped or tightly controlled VPC/on-prem deployment for portions of the workflow (document ingestion, PHI processing).
- Strict egress restrictions: outbound connections only to a small allowlist (no public internet access from processing nodes).
- Need for HSM/KMS integration and audit logging for key operations.

Goals we discussed:
- Proof-of-concept: private VPC deployment in your Azure tenant with limited egress and KMS integration.
- Confirm network architecture and required firewall rules so infra can validate feasibility.
- Security deep-dive with your architecture & security teams next week (we recommended a 60–90 min session).

What Redwood can provide / our assumptions:
- Private deployment options: VPC-hosted managed control plane + customer-managed data plane (can support HSM/KMS + VNet peering).
- Offline/air-gapped option for fully isolated environments (requires on-prem appliance or customer-provided jump hosts for updates).
- We will produce a short network allowlist and a deployment checklist for your infra team.

Action items:
1) Alex / Security: share a current network diagram (VNET/subnets, firewalls) and any outbound allowlist constraints (we need NAT/gw details).
2) HealthTech: complete and return the attached security questionnaire to help us scope SOC2/KMS needs (attachment: HealthTech_Security_Questionnaire.pdf).
3) Redwood: Marissa to schedule security deep-dive and prepare a deployment checklist + scoped BOM for on-prem components.
4) Schedule: propose next steps once we have the diagram — target security deep-dive for next Tue/Wed.

Attachments: HealthTech_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (attached).

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthtech.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Security <security@healthtech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HealthTech private VPC/disconnected deployment (network & compliance needs)

Camila — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming a few clarifications from our side and attaching the network diagram you asked for.

Clarifications / constraints:
- We have a hard requirement that processing nodes handling PHI cannot have any public egress except to a tightly allowlisted set of endpoints.
- For PII-deidentification flows we can open limited egress for updates, but production processing must be air-gapped behind our perimeter.
- KMS is managed by us via an HSM cluster; any integration needs to support customer-side key management.

Attached: healthtech_network_diagram.png (public subnet, private processing subnet, firewall rules).

Next steps from our side:
1) Security team to validate Redwood's checklist once shared.
2) We’ll share a minimal list of allowed external endpoints (expect that by EOD Monday).
3) Please confirm whether Redwood’s air-gapped option requires on-prem hardware or whether a customer-managed jump host in our VPC is sufficient.

Alex
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
HealthTech Systems
alex.johnson@healthtech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthtech.com>, IT Security <security@healthtech.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HealthTech private VPC/disconnected deployment (network & compliance needs)

Hi Alex / Security team — thanks for the diagram, that helps a lot. A few technical notes and answers to your questions:

1) Air-gapped vs. customer-managed jump host:
- Our "air-gapped" package can be delivered as an on-prem appliance for fully isolated sites. For cloud VPC deployments where you want zero internet egress from processing nodes, we support a customer-managed jump host pattern: control plane updates are pushed by the customer through an approved bastion/jump host that we sign and verify. This avoids shipping hardware but preserves isolation.

2) KMS/HSM integration:
- We support customer-managed KMS via standard KMIP and commonly used cloud HSM integrations (Azure Key Vault HSM + BYOK). Our deployment team will work with your security engineers to exchange certs and ensure keys never leave customer-managed hardware.

3) Network allowlist & ports:
- From initial review, we'll need the following minimal egress to allow Redwood health checks and optional telemetry (if you opt in):
  - outbound TCP 443 to our control-plane endpoints (can be limited by IP/cname)
  - NTP (UDP 123) to your internal time servers (or we can use internal NTP).

If telemetry is not allowed, we can disable telemetry collection and rely on customer-side logs.

4) Next steps / proposed plan:
- Marissa to run a quick internal feasibility check with the infra team and produce a 1-page deployment checklist by EOD Monday.
- Camila to schedule the security deep-dive for Wed (60–90min).
- Provide us with the list of allowed endpoints and any extra compliance docs (we'll correlate with SOC2 items).

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/HT-4582) and shared Drive with draft deployment options: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-healthtech-security

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HealthTech private VPC/disconnected deployment (network & compliance needs)

Alex — perfect, thank you. Per Marissa's note, we'll:

- Produce the deployment checklist and start the feasibility runbook (Marissa / Michael).
- Disable telemetry by default for your environment; if you later opt in, we can enable filtered telemetry via the bastion.
- Prepare the scope doc for KMS/HSM integration and share certificate-exchange steps ahead of the security call.

I've scheduled the security deep-dive for Wednesday, 2027-08-04 at 10:00 AM PT (60 minutes). Invite should be in your calendar — please accept or propose a new time.

Attached for your reference: redwood_private_vpc_options.pdf (brief doc on deployment variants).

Looking forward to the call.

Thanks,
Camila
